current_object.title: Total charge, dipole moment, Cartesian moments and traceless quadrupole of a static charge distribution
current_object.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), inherited from the Lebesgue interface used below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let the laboratory region, its chart, its spatial Euclidean structure and its units be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]], and let $\delta_{ij}$ be the Kronecker symbol in the $\delta$-orthonormal basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of the frame, with $|y|$ the Euclidean norm of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. This definition assigns **source moments** to a static charge distribution in the fixed-time reading of [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] (d) and (e). Two branches are declared.

(a) [Absolutely continuous branch] Let $a>0$ and let $\rho\in L^1(\mathbb R^3)$ be real ([[def-l-one-of-a-measure]]) and vanish $\lambda_3$-almost everywhere outside the closed ball $\overline B_a(0)=\{y:|y|\le a\}$ ([[def-metric-ball]], [[def-measure-null-set-and-almost-everywhere]]). The **total charge** $Q$, the **dipole moment** $p$, the **degree-$l$ Cartesian moments** $M_{i_1\dots i_l}$ and the **traceless quadrupole** $Q_{ij}$ are
$$Q:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\rho\,d\lambda_3,\qquad p_i:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}y_i\,\rho(y)\,d\lambda_3(y),$$
$$M_{i_1\dots i_l}:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}y_{i_1}\cdots y_{i_l}\,\rho(y)\,d\lambda_3(y)\quad(l\ge0),\qquad Q_{ij}:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\bigl(3y_iy_j-|y|^2\delta_{ij}\bigr)\rho(y)\,d\lambda_3(y),$$
with $M^{(0)}:=Q$ and $M_i:=p_i$, indices in $\{1,2,3\}$, units C, C m, C m$^l$ and C m$^2$, and integrals in the sense of [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]] and [[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]]. Each integral is absolutely convergent: since $\rho=0$ $\lambda_3$-a.e. off $\overline B_a(0)$ and the maps $y\mapsto y_{i_1}\cdots y_{i_l}$ and $y\mapsto 3y_iy_j-|y|^2\delta_{ij}$ are bounded there by $a^l$ and $4a^2$, the integrands are dominated $\lambda_3$-a.e. by $a^l|\rho|$ and $4a^2|\rho|$, which lie in $L^1$ ([[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]], [[thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]). The traceless quadrupole is traceless, $\sum_iQ_{ii}=0$, since $\sum_i(3y_i^2-|y|^2)=0$ pointwise ([[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]]), and replacing $\rho$ by an equal $\lambda_3$-a.e. density changes no moment ([[thm-the-lebesgue-integral-respects-almost-everywhere-equality]]).

(b) [General locally integrable branch] If instead $\rho\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^3)$ is real and $\int_{\mathbb R^3}|y|^l|\rho(y)|\,d\lambda_3(y)<\infty$ for a given $l\ge0$, then the degree-$l$ Cartesian moments of the same formula are absolutely convergent and defined; if the $L$-th absolute moment is finite for some $L\ge0$, then every degree $l\le L$ is defined. No compact support and no $L^1$-membership is assumed in this branch.

(c) [Finite system of stationary point charges] Let $N\ge0$, $x_1,\dots,x_N\in\mathbb R^3$ and $q_1,\dots,q_N\in\mathbb R$ be charge parameters ([[def-em-sources]] (a)), read as the stationary point charges $q_k\delta_{x_k}$ in the fixed-time reading of [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] (e). Define
$$Q:=\sum_{k=1}^Nq_k,\qquad p:=\sum_{k=1}^Nq_kx_k,\qquad M_{i_1\dots i_l}:=\sum_{k=1}^Nq_k\,x_{k,i_1}\cdots x_{k,i_l},\qquad Q_{ij}:=\sum_{k=1}^Nq_k\bigl(3x_{k,i}x_{k,j}-|x_k|^2\delta_{ij}\bigr),$$
finite sums in the sense of [[def-finite-sum]] ([[lem-finite-sum-laws]]); again $\sum_iQ_{ii}=0$. The points need not be distinct; charges at a common point add.

(d) [Reference point and scope] Every moment is computed about the chart origin of [[def-em-lab-geometry]]; this origin is part of the definition. These are source moments of a prescribed static distribution — not momenta, rest masses, intrinsic spins, self-energies or dynamical quantities — and no field, force, equation of motion, equilibrium or empirical claim is made here; the static regime in which the source is read is the adopted idealisation of [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] (f).
current_object.strategy: An explicit type/domain/convention definition with its well-definedness checks displayed in the clauses: absolute convergence and null-set irrelevance in (a), the finite-absolute-moment hypothesis in (b), and the finite-sum identities in (c). The mathematical inputs are the Lebesgue interface ([[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]], [[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]], [[def-l-one-of-a-measure]]), the pointwise bounds $|y_{i_1}\cdots y_{i_l}|\le a^l$ and $|3y_iy_j-|y|^2\delta_{ij}|\le4a^2$ on $\overline B_a(0)$, the triangle and monotonicity estimates ([[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]], [[thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]), linearity of the integral ([[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]]), null-set irrelevance ([[thm-the-lebesgue-integral-respects-almost-everywhere-equality]]) and finite-sum algebra ([[def-finite-sum]], [[lem-finite-sum-laws]]). The physical reading uses only the fixed-time dictionary of [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] (d), (e); no Choice beyond the declared $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of the measure interface is used.

current_object.title: Explicit mathematical hypothesis/convention examples
current_object.statement: Three exact boundary checks. (i) The sphere trace $f(n)=n_3$ is the trace of the homogeneous degree-one harmonic polynomial $u(x)=x_3$, so the ball boundary branch of [[thm-em-spherical-multipole-basis]] applies to it; the simultaneous conditions $\Delta u=0$ in the unit ball $B_1$ and $\partial_nu=1$ on $S^2$ are incompatible, because the divergence theorem gives $0=\int_{B_1}\Delta u\,dx=\int_{S^2}\partial_nu\,d\sigma=\sigma(S^2)=4\pi$. (ii) For the coefficient $\varepsilon=1$ on $\{x_1<0\}$ and $\varepsilon=2$ on $\{x_1>0\}$, the function $u=x_1$ on the first side and $u=x_1/2$ on the second is continuous and locally $H^1$, and $\varepsilon\partial_1u\equiv1$, so $-\operatorname{div}(\varepsilon\nabla u)=0$ weakly although $u$ is not $C^1$: its first derivative jumps from $1$ to $1/2$ across the interface. Hence the smooth-coefficient statements of [[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]] cannot be extended to this piecewise-constant case, and the correct conclusion there is the piecewise regularity recorded by that item, not a global $C^1$ or $C^\infty$-on-the-closure statement. (iii) The same wild-coefficient configuration is a hypothesis boundary for the smooth-domain spectral completeness of [[thm-em-waveguide-spectral-completeness]]: its coefficients and interfaces are exactly the ones excluded from the smooth $C^\infty$ PEC/smooth-domain hypotheses, and the explicit solution shows that a global classical conclusion fails while the weak $H^1$ formulation remains valid. All three parts are exact finite computations or classical divergence-theorem evaluations; they assert no physical interpretation.
current_object.strategy:
Direct computations. Part (i): $\Delta x_3=0$ and $
abla x_3=e_3$, so on the unit sphere $\partial_nx_3=e_3\cdot n=n_3$; if a function were harmonic in $B_1$ with $\partial_nu=1$ on $S^2$, the divergence theorem [[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-c-one-euclidean-domains]] applied to $
abla u$ (a $C^1$ field) would give $0=\int_{B_1}\Delta u\,d\lambda=\int_{S^2}\partial_nu\,d\sigma$, while the polar-coordinates formula [[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]] and the defining normalisation give $\sigma(S^2)=3\lambda_3(B_1)=4\pi$; the contradiction $0=4\pi$ proves incompatibility, and the Laplacian is that of [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]. Part (ii): on each open half-space the field $\varepsilon
abla u$ is the constant $(1,0,0)$, so its distributional divergence is zero ([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]): testing $-\operatorname{div}(\varepsilon
abla u)$ against a compactly supported smooth test function and integrating by parts reduces to $\int_{\mathbb R^3}\partial_1\varphi\cdot(-1)\,dx=0$ for a constant field. The function $u$ is continuous because $x_1$ and $x_1/2$ both tend to $0$ at the interface, its distributional first derivatives are the locally integrable functions equal to $1,0,0$ respectively $1/2,0,0$ on the two sides ([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]), and these representatives jump at $x_1=0$, so $u$ is $H^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$ but not $C^1$. Part (iii): this is the statement that the excluded case is excluded: the smooth coefficients and smooth interfaces required by [[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]] and by the smooth-domain class of [[thm-em-waveguide-spectral-completeness]] fail, while the displayed weak solution exists and is not smooth on the closure. No physical postulate, measurement or empirical claim is used.

current_object.title: Explicit mathematical hypothesis and convention examples for the elementary prerequisites
current_object.statement: Take $D=[0,1]^2$, $a\in C^2(I)$ with $a>0$, $r(u,v,t)=(a(t)u,a(t)v,0)$, $B=e_3$ and $v=(a'/a)(x_1,x_2,0)$. The parametrized flux is $a^2$, so its derivative is $2aa'$. The fixed-time surface integral of $B_t$ is $0$, while $\operatorname{curl}(v\times B)=-2(a'/a)e_3$; patch Stokes therefore gives $\oint(v\times B)\cdot d\mathbf l=-2aa'$, exactly the sign in the moving-flux lemma. Treating this moving patch as fixed would falsely give zero. All fields and maps are smooth at the stated regularity, and no singular support is involved.
current_object.strategy: Verify each display by direct computation at the stated regularity. The example checks the sign convention of the moving-flux lemma and the necessity of the motion term; it does not assert any physical law.

current_object.title: Four stationary point charges with vanishing total charge and dipole moment and traceless quadrupole diag(6qa^2,-6qa^2,0)
current_object.strategy: Insert the four points into the finite sums of [[def-em-electric-moments]] (c) and use $\delta$-orthonormality of the frame basis: $Q=q+q-q-q=0$ and $p=q(ae_1)+q(-ae_1)+(-q)(ae_2)+(-q)(-ae_2)=0$. For (a), the configuration is invariant under $x\mapsto-x$ with the charge of each point preserved ($+q$ at $\pm ae_1$ and $-q$ at $\pm ae_2$), so pairing each point with its image and reindexing the finite sum ([[def-finite-sum]], [[lem-finite-sum-laws]]) gives $M_{i_1\dots i_{2k+1}}=\sum_k q_k x_k^{\otimes(2k+1)}=0$: the terms at $x$ and $-x$ contribute $q\bigl(1+(-1)^{2k+1}\bigr)x^{\otimes(2k+1)}=0$. For (b), direct substitution gives $M_{ij}=q(ae_1)_i(ae_1)_j+q(-ae_1)_i(-ae_1)_j-q(ae_2)_i(ae_2)_j-q(-ae_2)_i(-ae_2)_j=2qa^2\bigl(e_{1i}e_{1j}-e_{2i}e_{2j}\bigr)=2qa^2\bigl(\delta_{i1}\delta_{j1}-\delta_{i2}\delta_{j2}\bigr)$, whose trace $2qa^2(1-1)$ vanishes; the components are read in the $\delta$-orthonormal basis ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]). For (c), use $Q_{ij}=\sum_kq_k\bigl(3x_{k,i}x_{k,j}-|x_k|^2\delta_{ij}\bigr)=3M_{ij}-\delta_{ij}\sum_kq_k|x_k|^2$ from [[def-em-electric-moments]] (c); each $|x_k|=a$, so $\sum_kq_k|x_k|^2=a^2(q+q-q-q)=0$ and $Q_{ij}=3M_{ij}=6qa^2\bigl(\delta_{i1}\delta_{j1}-\delta_{i2}\delta_{j2}\bigr)$, with trace $6qa^2(1-1)=0$; the reference-point independence for $Q=p=0$ is clause (d) of [[pthm-em-moment-origin-change]]. The equality $|x_k|=a$ for $x_k=\pm ae_1,\pm ae_2$ uses $\delta(e_r,e_r)=1$ ([[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]) and the Euclidean norm of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]] (with [[thm-cauchy-schwarz-and-the-euclidean-norm]] for reading norms of coordinate vectors). Clause (d) records that no field, energy or dynamics is computed. No Choice axiom is used: all sums are finite ([[lem-finite-sum-laws]]).

current_object.title: Exact two-charge dipole potential, its moments and the explicit far-field remainder
current_object.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), inherited from the cited distribution and Lebesgue interfaces ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $q\in\mathbb R$ and $d\in\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$, put $a:=|d|/2$, and let the source be the two stationary point charges $+q$ at $d/2$ and $-q$ at $-d/2$ (charge parameters in coulombs and the constant $\varepsilon_0$ of [[def-em-si-conventions]]), with fixed-time reading $q\delta_{d/2}-q\delta_{-d/2}$ ([[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] (e), [[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]]). Define, with arbitrary values at the two points,
$$\varphi(x):=\frac{q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0|x-d/2|}-\frac{q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0|x+d/2|}\qquad\bigl(x\notin\{d/2,-d/2\}\bigr).$$
Then:
(a) [Exact potential and equations] $\varphi$ is locally integrable on $\mathbb R^3$ and of class $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R^3\setminus\{d/2,-d/2\}$; with $E:=-\nabla\varphi$ on that set ([[def-em-fields]]), the pair $(E,0)$ satisfies the distributional pure electrostatic equations
$$\operatorname{div}E=\frac{q\,\delta_{d/2}-q\,\delta_{-d/2}}{\varepsilon_0},\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=0\qquad\text{in }\mathcal D'(\mathbb R^3)$$
of the fixed-time dictionary of [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] (e) ([[pthm-em-coulomb-solution]] (d) for each point charge, added by linearity of distributional differentiation: [[def-distribution]], [[def-distributional-derivative]], [[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]], [[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]], [[thm-distributional-differentiation-is-continuous-and-commutes]]);
(b) [Moments] in the finite-sum branch of [[def-em-electric-moments]] (c) about the chart origin of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], $Q=0$, $p=qd$, every even Cartesian moment vanishes, $M_{i_1\dots i_{2k+1}}=2q\,(d/2)_{i_1}\cdots(d/2)_{i_{2k+1}}$ for every $k\ge0$, and the traceless quadrupole vanishes, $Q_{ij}=0$;
(c) [Exact far-field comparison] for every $x$ with $r:=|x|\ge2a=|d|$, the exact difference obeys the expansion form of [[pthm-em-electric-dipole-expansion]] with the point-pair total variation in place of $\|\rho\|_1$:
$$\varphi(x)=\frac{p\cdot x}{4\pi\varepsilon_0r^3}+R(x),\qquad |R(x)|\le\frac{16\,a^2\,(|q|+|{-q}|)}{4\pi\varepsilon_0r^3}=\frac{8|q|a^2}{\pi\varepsilon_0r^3};$$
(d) [Comparison with the compact-density theorem] the hypothesis of [[pthm-em-electric-dipole-expansion]] is an $L^1$ density and is not met by the point pair, so that theorem is not applied to it; the identity and bound of (c) are proved directly for the two kernels by the twice-fundamental-theorem computation used in that theorem's remainder, and the leading term, the $a^2$ decay and the appearance of the total variation agree with the compact-density expansion;
(e) [Scope] the potential and the distributional equations are stated for the idealised singular source; no self-energy, self-force, dynamics, bound-state, stability or empirical claim is made for the pair.
current_object.strategy:
The individual point-charge objects and their distributional identities are those of [[pthm-em-coulomb-solution]] (d): for a charge $q'$ at $x_0$, $\varphi_{q'}$ is locally integrable, $C^\infty$ off $x_0$, $E_{q'}=-\nabla\varphi_{q'}$ off $x_0$, and $\operatorname{div}E_{q'}=(q'/\varepsilon_0)\delta_{x_0}$, $\operatorname{curl}E_{q'}=0$ in $\mathcal D'(\mathbb R^3)$. Summing the two locally integrable potentials gives the displayed $\varphi$ (values at the two points are immaterial, [[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]], [[thm-the-lebesgue-integral-respects-almost-everywhere-equality]]), and the distributional derivative of the sum is the sum of the distributional derivatives ([[thm-distributional-differentiation-is-continuous-and-commutes]], [[def-distribution]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]); adding the two point-charge identities componentwise and using [[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]] gives (a), and the fixed-time dictionary is [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] (e). For (b), substitute into the finite sums of [[def-em-electric-moments]] (c): $Q=q+(-q)=0$, $p=q(d/2)+(-q)(-d/2)=qd$, and $M_{i_1\dots i_l}=q(d/2)^{\otimes l}+(-q)(-d/2)^{\otimes l}=q\bigl(1-(-1)^l\bigr)(d/2)^{\otimes l}$, which vanishes for even $l$ and equals $2q(d/2)^{\otimes l}$ for odd $l$; since $M^{(2)}=0$ and $\sum_kq_k|x_k|^2=qa^2+(-q)a^2=0$, the traceless quadrupole $Q_{ij}=3M_{ij}-\delta_{ij}\sum_kq_k|x_k|^2$ vanishes, consistent with the reference-point independence clause of [[pthm-em-moment-origin-change]] (d) because $Q=p=0$ ([[def-finite-sum]], [[lem-finite-sum-laws]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). For (c), apply the twice-fundamental-theorem remainder computation to each of the two kernels directly, since the density theorem does not apply to the pair. Write $h_y(s):=|x-sy|^{-1}$ for $y\in\{d/2,-d/2\}$; for $r\ge2a$ and $s\in[0,1]$ one has $|x-sy|\ge r-a\ge r/2$, the chain rule gives $h_y'(s)=\frac{(x-sy)\cdot y}{|x-sy|^3}$ and $h_y''(s)=-\frac{|y|^2}{|x-sy|^3}+3\frac{((x-sy)\cdot y)^2}{|x-sy|^5}$ with $|h_y''(s)|\le4|y|^2/|x-sy|^3\le32|y|^2/r^3=32a^2/r^3$, and the identity $h_y(1)-h_y(0)-h_y'(0)=\int_0^1(1-t)h_y''(t)\,dt$ is the fundamental theorem applied to $\frac{d}{dt}\bigl[(1-t)h_y'(t)+h_y(t)\bigr]=(1-t)h_y''(t)$ ([[thm-newton-leibniz-with-interior-derivative]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]], [[lem-every-norm-on-rn-is-continuous-for-the-euclidean-metric]], [[def-metric-ball]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]), so $h_y(1)=1/r+x\cdot y/r^3+R_y(x)$ with $|R_y(x)|\le16|y|^2/r^3$ ([[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]], [[thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]). Substituting the two kernels with their charges and using $|y|=a$, with the two linear terms adding to $q(x\cdot d)/r^3=p\cdot x/r^3$,
$$\varphi(x)-\frac{p\cdot x}{4\pi\varepsilon_0r^3}=\frac{q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\bigl(R_{d/2}(x)-R_{-d/2}(x)\bigr),\qquad \Bigl|\varphi(x)-\frac{p\cdot x}{4\pi\varepsilon_0r^3}\Bigr|\le\frac{|q|(16a^2+16a^2)}{4\pi\varepsilon_0r^3}=\frac{32|q|a^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0r^3}=\frac{8|q|a^2}{\pi\varepsilon_0r^3},$$
which is (c); reading it against [[pthm-em-electric-dipole-expansion]] gives (d). The two vector terms use the Euclidean inner product and norm ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[thm-cauchy-schwarz-and-the-euclidean-norm]]); no differentiation of $\varphi$ beyond the off-pole gradient is used and no value at the poles is asserted. For (e), no field energy is computed and the self-energy of a point charge is not claimed finite here. Countable Choice is used only through the cited distribution and Lebesgue interfaces; the potential and field of each charge are the idealised singular objects of [[pthm-em-coulomb-solution]] (d) and [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] (e).

current_object.title: Ball Poisson series: interior convergence, boundary data and the Poisson kernel
current_object.statement: Let $f\in L^2(S^2,d\Omega)$ with harmonic coefficients $f_{lm}$ in an orthonormal basis of the spherical-harmonic lemma ([[lem-em-spherical-harmonic-basis-and-addition]]), and for $0\le r<1$ set $u(rn)=\sum_{l,m}r^lf_{lm}Y_{lm}(n)$ (the $l=0$ term being the constant value at $r=0$). Then the series and all its derivatives converge uniformly on every closed smaller ball, $u$ is harmonic there ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]), $u(r\,\cdot)\to f$ in $L^2(S^2)$ as $r\uparrow1$, and $u$ is the unique harmonic function on the unit ball with $\sup_{r<1}\|u(r\,\cdot)\|_{L^2}<\infty$ and $L^2$ boundary limit $f$. For continuous $f$ the same function is $$u(rn)=\int_{S^2}\frac{1-r^2}{4\pi|rn-n'|^3}f(n')\,d\Omega(n'),$$ it extends continuously to the closed ball with boundary value $f$, and the kernel is positive of total mass one. This is the stated ball boundary branch; generic smooth-domain classical regularity remains a separate obligation.
current_object.strategy: The addition theorem of the spherical-harmonic lemma gives $\sum_m|Y_{lm}(n)|^2=(2l+1)/(4\pi)$ ([[lem-em-spherical-harmonic-basis-and-addition]]); Cauchy-Schwarz over $m$ and then $l$ ([[cor-cauchy-schwarz-inequality-for-l-two]]) bounds the absolute tail at fixed $r\le r_0<1$ by $\|f\|_2[\sum_{l>N}r_0^{2l}(2l+1)/(4\pi)]^{1/2}\to0$. On a smaller closed ball, apply the interior derivative estimates to each harmonic partial-sum difference on balls of fixed radius inside an intermediate ball ([[thm-interior-derivative-estimates-for-harmonic-functions]]): every derivative is uniformly bounded by the already vanishing uniform bound on the partial sums, so all derivatives are uniformly Cauchy; the limits identify the derivatives of the limit and $\Delta u=0$ ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]). Orthogonal expansion gives $\|u(r\,\cdot)-f\|_2^2=\sum_{l,m}(1-r^l)^2|f_{lm}|^2\to0$ by dominated convergence of the summable bound $4\sum|f_{lm}|^2$. For uniqueness, a smooth harmonic $v$ has radial coefficients solving $v_{lm}''+2r^{-1}v_{lm}'-l(l+1)r^{-2}v_{lm}=0$ by the polar Laplacian and $\Delta_{S^2}Y_{lm}=-l(l+1)Y_{lm}$; the two solutions are $r^l$ and $r^{-l-1}$, and smoothness at the origin excludes the second, so a specified $L^2$ boundary limit fixes the coefficient $f_{lm}$ and completeness gives equality. Summing the zonal addition kernels with weights $r^l$ and applying $(1+2r\partial_r)$ to the generating function of the zonal lemma gives the displayed Poisson kernel; it is positive, and its integral is one because only the normalised constant harmonic survives integration. For continuous $f$ uniform boundary convergence follows by splitting the integral into a small spherical neighbourhood of $n$ (where uniform continuity controls the error) and its complement (whose kernel mass tends to zero uniformly).

current_object.title: Legendre polynomials from a convergent zonal kernel: generating function and exterior expansion
current_object.statement: For $z\in[-1,1]$ define the real polynomial $P_l(z)=\pi^{-1}\int_0^\pi\bigl[z+i\sqrt{1-z^2}\,\cos\theta\bigr]^l\,d\theta$, $l\in\mathbb N_0$. Then $P_l$ is a real polynomial of degree at most $l$ with $|P_l(z)|\le1$ on $[-1,1]$, $P_l(1)=1$, and for $|q|<1$ the series $\sum_{l\ge0}q^lP_l(z)$ converges absolutely and uniformly on $[-1,1]$ with $$(1-2qz+q^2)^{-1/2}=\sum_{l=0}^{\infty}q^lP_l(z),$$ where the branch is the analytic square root equal to $1$ at $q=0$ ([[def-series-of-real-functions]], [[thm-weierstrass-m-test-for-function-series]]). Consequently, for $r>|y|$ with $n=x/|x|$ and $N\in\mathbb N_0$, $\bigl|\,|x-y|^{-1}-\sum_{l=0}^{N}|y|^l|x|^{-l-1}P_l(n\cdot y/|y|)\bigr|\le|y|^{N+1}|x|^{-N-2}(1-|y|/|x|)^{-1}$, uniformly on $|y|\le a<r$ (with $y=0$ interpreted by the zero higher terms), and after integrating against an $L^1$ source the corresponding multipole expansion converges with that error times its $L^1$ norm. On an observation compact set disjoint from $\overline{B_a(0)}$ every fixed spatial derivative series converges uniformly, by analyticity of the kernel in the parameter $y$ ([[def-complex-domain]], [[thm-identity-theorem-holomorphic-functions]], [[thm-differentiation-under-the-integral-sign]]). This lemma supplies the convergent zonal kernel; it does not by itself prove a spherical $L^2$ basis or boundary convergence.
current_object.strategy: Realness and the degree bound follow by expanding the finite power and integrating the odd cosine moments away; $|P_l(z)|\le1$ uses $|z+i\sqrt{1-z^2}\cos\theta|\le1$. For the generating function integrate the geometric series $\sum_{l\ge0}[q(z+i\sqrt{1-z^2}\cos\theta)]^l=(1-qz-iq\sqrt{1-z^2}\cos\theta)^{-1}$ termwise over $\theta$; the geometric ratio has modulus $\le|q|<1$ uniformly in $\theta$, so the Weierstrass $M$-test gives uniform convergence and termwise integration gives the coefficient representation $P_l$. The integral $\int_0^\pi(a+b\cos\theta)^{-1}d\theta=\pi/\sqrt{a^2-b^2}$ for $a>|b|$ is computed by the tangent substitution $u=\tan(\theta/2)$ ([[thm-substitution]], [[thm-principal-inverse-tangent-calculus]]). Substituting $a=1-qz$, $b=-iq\sqrt{1-z^2}$ gives $\pi(1-2qz+q^2)^{-1/2}$. Both sides are holomorphic in $(q,z)$ near the real values with $|q|<1$, where $1-2qz+q^2$ never vanishes, so the identity extends by the identity theorem for holomorphic functions ([[def-complex-domain]], [[thm-identity-theorem-holomorphic-functions]]). Substituting $q=|y|/r$, $z=n\cdot y/|y|$ and using $|P_l|\le1$ gives the geometric tail bound for the displayed kernel expansion. For derivative convergence on a compact observation set, the kernel is holomorphic in a neighbourhood of the parameter domain bounded away from its zeros; Cauchy-type uniform bounds on a slightly larger complex disk ([[thm-differentiation-under-the-integral-sign]]) bound every fixed spatial derivative of the series terms by a polynomial in $l$ times $(a/r)^l$, and the ratio test gives uniform convergence of each derivative series. No asymptotic large-$l$ formula is used.

current_object.title: Monopole-dipole expansion with an explicit remainder for compactly supported $L^1$ densities
current_object.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$). Let $a>0$ and let $\rho\in L^1(\mathbb R^3)$ vanish outside $\{y:\lvert y\rvert\le a\}$. Put $Q:=\int\rho$, $p:=\int y\,\rho(y)\,dy$ and $\lVert\rho\rVert_1:=\int\lvert\rho\rvert$. Then for every $x$ with $r:=\lvert x\rvert\ge2a>0$, $$\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{\rho(y)}{\lvert x-y\rvert}\,dy=\frac Qr+\frac{p\cdot x}{r^3}+R(x),\qquad \lvert R(x)\rvert\le\frac{16\,a^2\lVert\rho\rVert_1}{r^3}.$$
current_object.strategy: Set $h(s)=\lvert x-sy\rvert^{-1}$; $h$ is $C^2$ on $[0,1]$ and the identity $h(1)-h(0)-h'(0)=\int_0^1(1-s)h''(s)\,ds$ follows from the fundamental theorem applied to $\frac{d}{ds}[(1-s)h'(s)+h(s)]=(1-s)h''(s)$. Because $\lvert x-sy\rvert\ge r-a\ge r/2$ for $r\ge2a$, one has $\lvert h''(s)\rvert\le4\lvert y\rvert^2/(r-a)^3\le32\lvert y\rvert^2/r^3$, and integrating against $\lvert\rho\rvert$ gives the bound with $C=16$, which is permissible but not sharp. The published far-field theorem supplies the leading $Q/r$ term only.

current_object.title: Uniqueness of the outgoing scalar Helmholtz solution with a smooth obstacle
current_object.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the modal DtN/trace suppliers, covering the Countable Choice used by the local UCP supplier. Let $O\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded open set with $C^\infty$ boundary ([[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]) whose exterior $D=\mathbb R^3\setminus\overline O$ is connected, let $k>0$, and let $R>0$ with $\overline O\subset B_R(0)$. Suppose $u$ is $C^\infty$ on $\overline D$, solves $(\Delta+k^2)u=0$ on $D$ with the Euclidean Laplacian $\Delta$ ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]), vanishes on $\partial O$, and is outgoing in the class of [[lem-em-sphere-outgoing-dirichlet-to-neumann-map]]: its trace $f=u|_{S_R}$ lies in $H^{1/2}(S_R)$ and its normal derivative on $S_R$ is $T_Rf$ in the weak trace sense of that lemma. Then $u=0$ on $D$. No decay rate, asymptotic expansion or pointwise Sommerfeld formula beyond the stated outgoing class is assumed.
current_object.strategy: Green's identity on the truncated exterior. Apply the first Green identity [[cor-first-green-identity-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]] to $u$ and its complex conjugate on the bounded $C^1$ domain $D\cap B_R$, whose boundary consists of $\partial O$ and $S_R$: the volume integral is the real number $\int_{D\cap B_R}(|\nabla u|^2-k^2|u|^2)\,dx$, and the inner boundary contributes zero because $u=0$ on $\partial O$. The full boundary pairing equals that real volume integral, so its imaginary part is zero; its real part need not vanish. Thus $\operatorname{Im}\langle T_Rf,f\rangle=0$. By [[lem-em-sphere-outgoing-dirichlet-to-neumann-map]] applied to $f$ the imaginary part is $\operatorname{Im}\langle T_Rf,f\rangle=\sum_{l,m}(\operatorname{Im}t_l)|f_{lm}|^2$ with $\operatorname{Im}t_l>0$ for every $l$; the already established zero imaginary pairing and the strictly positive modal coefficients force every $f_{lm}=0$. Consequently the outgoing exterior series of that lemma, which is the unique outgoing finite-local-energy solution with trace $f$ on $S_R$, vanishes on $\{r>R\}$; combined with $u=0$ on $\partial O$ the function $u$ vanishes on the complement of $D\cap\overline B_R$. On $D$ the real and imaginary parts of $u$ are $H^2_{\mathrm{loc}}$ solutions of $\Delta w=Vw$ with the bounded coefficient $V=-k^2$, so [[thm-bounded-potential-weak-unique-continuation-in-three-dimensions]] applies to each of them on the connected open $D$: each vanishes on the nonempty open set $D\cap\{r>R\}$, hence on $D$. Therefore $u=0$ on $D$. No finite experimental observation or physical postulate is used.

current_object.title: Outgoing source Helmholtz field: fundamental solution, Fraunhofer and Fresnel error terms
current_object.statement: For $k>0$ define $G_k(x)=e^{ik|x|}/(4\pi|x|)$ off the origin, a locally integrable complex function. Then $$(-\Delta-k^2)G_k=\delta_0$$ distributionally. For a finite complex measure $\alpha$ supported in $B_a(0)$, the field $u=G_k*\alpha$ is smooth outside the support, solves $(\Delta+k^2)u=0$ there and is outgoing: for $x=rn$, $r\ge2a$, $$u(rn)=\frac{e^{ikr}}{4\pi r}\int e^{-ikn\cdot y}\,d\alpha(y)+O\!\Bigl(\frac{\|\alpha\|_{\mathrm{TV}}}{r}\Bigl[\frac{a}{r}+\frac{ka^2}{r}\Bigr]\Bigr)$$ uniformly in direction, and $r(\partial_ru-iku)=O(r^{-1})$ uniformly. For a planar aperture $y=(y_1,y_2,0)$ with observation $x=(\xi_1,\xi_2,z)$, $z>0$, $|\xi|\le b$, $a+b\ll z$, the Fresnel approximation replaces $R=|x-y|$ by $z+|\xi-y|^2/(2z)$ and $1/R$ by $1/z$ with phase error $O(k(a+b)^4/z^3)$ and relative amplitude error $O((a+b)^2/z^2)$, hence absolute field error $O(\|\alpha\|_{\mathrm{TV}}z^{-1}[(a+b)^2/z^2+k(a+b)^4/z^3])$. Aperture data are an explicitly specified scalar source, not asserted to be the unknown exact Maxwell boundary traces, and no uniqueness or existence for arbitrary obstacle boundary data is claimed.
current_object.strategy: For radial $f(r)$ one has $\Delta f=f''+2f'/r$ by direct coordinate differentiation of $\partial_ir=x_i/r$ ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]), and inserting $f=G_k$ gives $(\Delta+k^2)f=0$ for $r>0$. For the distributional identity excise a ball $B_\delta$ inside a compact test integration; the second Green identity ([[cor-second-green-identity-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]]) on the excised domain cancels the $k^2$ terms and leaves the inner flux, where $G_k=1/(4\pi\delta)+O(1)$ and $\partial_rG_k=-1/(4\pi\delta^2)+O(1)$: the derivative-test boundary term is $O(\delta)$ and the leading unit flux multiplies $\psi(0)$, while the local $k^2G_k$ integral is $O(\delta^2)$; the limit is $\delta_0$ with the displayed sign. Off-support smoothness and all derivatives follow from the positive separation of compact observation and source sets, with differentiation under the source integral. For the Fraunhofer error write $R=|rn-y|$ and use the norm expansion of the cited dipole-remainder technique ([[lem-em-coulomb-dipole-remainder]]): $|R-r+n\cdot y|\le Ca^2/r$ and $|r/R-1|\le Ca/r$; the exponential difference is bounded by $C r^{-1}(a/r+ka^2/r)$ via $|e^{i\theta}-1|\le|\theta|$, and integrating against the total variation of $\alpha$ with the integral triangle inequality ([[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]]) gives the displayed error; the outgoing relation follows from $\partial_rR=1+O(a^2/r^2)$ and $R^{-2}=O(r^{-2})$. The Fresnel estimate is the Taylor expansion of the norm with explicit remainder on the compact small-$s$ region $s=|\xi-y|^2/z^2$, using $|e^{i\theta}-1|\le|\theta|$.

current_object.title: Outgoing spherical trace and Dirichlet-to-Neumann map
current_object.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the explicitly used trace and weak Dirichlet-solvability suppliers. Let $k>0$ and $R>0$. Use the sphere-normalised basis $Y^R_{lm}(Rn):=R^{-1}Y_{lm}(n)$ on $S_R$, where $Y_{lm}$ is the complete normalised unit-sphere basis of the spherical-harmonic lemma ([[lem-em-spherical-harmonic-basis-and-addition]]) and the coefficients $t_l$ of the outgoing radial-function lemma ([[lem-em-outgoing-spherical-hankel-dtn-bounds]]). The map $$T_Rf=\sum_{l,m}t_l\,f_{lm}Y^R_{lm},\qquad f\in H^{1/2}(S_R),$$ is a bounded linear operator $H^{1/2}(S_R)\to H^{-1/2}(S_R)$ with $$\operatorname{Re}\langle T_Rf,f\rangle\le0,\qquad \operatorname{Im}\langle T_Rf,f\rangle=\sum_{l,m}(\operatorname{Im}t_l)|f_{lm}|^2>0\ \ (f\ne0).$$ It is precisely the outgoing scalar Helmholtz normal derivative at $r=R$: for every $f\in H^{1/2}(S_R)$ the function $u(rn)=\sum_{l,m}f_{lm}h_l(kr)/h_l(kR)\,R^{-1}Y_{lm}(n)$ for $r\ge R$ is the unique outgoing finite-local-energy exterior solution with trace $f$ on $S_R$ and normal derivative $T_Rf$ in the weak trace sense; it is smooth away from the sphere, and for smooth $f$ it satisfies the ordinary Sommerfeld condition. No uniform pointwise outgoing condition is asserted for arbitrary rough traces; the outgoing condition there is its modal/weak version. Here finite-local-energy means membership in $H^1(\{R<|x|<R_1\})$ for every finite $R_1>R$, with the $H^{1/2}$ trace on $S_R$; no global $H^1$ or global $L^2$ condition at infinity is imposed. The outgoing modal class consists of the displayed outgoing $h_l$ radial factors with no incoming partners; for rough traces this modal class is the definition, rather than a pointwise Sommerfeld assertion. Here the boundary Sobolev spaces are their complex versions (or complexifications of the real trace spaces), $f_{lm}=\int_{S_R}f\overline{Y^R_{lm}}\,d\sigma_R$, and the DtN dual pairing is linear in its first argument and conjugate-linear in its second.
current_object.strategy: The boundary norm of the fractional Sobolev space is equivalent, for fixed $R$, to $\sum_{l,m}(l+1)|f_{lm}|^2$: for finite harmonic data the harmonic ball extension $\sum_{l,m}(r/R)^lf_{lm}R^{-1}Y_{lm}(n)$ has Dirichlet energy $\sum(l/R)|f_{lm}|^2$ by the first Green identity ([[cor-first-green-identity-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]]) and normal differentiation, and $L^2$ ball norm $\sum R/(2l+3)|f_{lm}|^2$ with the sphere-normalised basis, so its $H^1$ norm is equivalent to $\sum(l+1)|f_{lm}|^2$. For arbitrary $H^{1/2}$ data the bounded right inverse and the weak harmonic Dirichlet solver of the prescribed-data lemma ([[lem-em-prescribed-fractional-dirichlet-existence]]) give a controlled harmonic $H^1$ extension; the harmonic coefficients and orthogonality of the ball Poisson series lemma ([[lem-em-ball-poisson-series-boundary-convergence]]) show the finite energy partial sums are bounded by its energy, giving both directions of the equivalence. The bounds $|t_l|\le(l+1)/R+k$ of the spherical Hankel lemma ([[lem-em-outgoing-spherical-hankel-dtn-bounds]]) make $T_R$ bounded into the dual weighted space, and the real and imaginary pairings converge with the stated signs, strict positivity following from $\operatorname{Im}t_l>0$ for every $l$. For the exterior realisation, define $u_{lm}(r)=f_{lm}h_l(kr)/h_l(kR)$, $r\ge R$; the finite polynomial positive formula gives $|h_l(kr)/h_l(kR)|\le R/r$ and, by the recurrence, geometric-in-$l$ radial ratios on every compact $r>R$ interval, so the series and all derivatives converge uniformly there, away from the sphere; the smoothness, the weak trace identification and the annular $H^1$ control follow from Green's identity for each mode on $[R,R+\delta]$ and the bounds above. Uniqueness: the general radial Helmholtz solutions are multiples of $h_l(kr)$ and its incoming partner, whose Wronskian is nonzero; Sommerfeld selects $h_l$, and harmonic completeness forces any smooth outgoing exterior solution to have exactly this map. The annular $H^1$ estimates are precisely the finite-local-energy condition; they do not assert global integrability at infinity. At $l=0$, a nonzero outgoing mode is proportional to $e^{ikr}/r$ and its global $L^2$ norm diverges, which confirms why no global energy condition is imposed. Both the ball and exterior radial extensions use $R^{-1}Y_{lm}(n)$ explicitly; the sphere-normalisation is $Y^R_{lm}(Rn)=R^{-1}Y_{lm}(n)$, giving the stated radial ball-norm factor $R/(2l+3)$ for the sphere-normalised coefficients. For complex boundary data, apply the real prescribed-trace/harmonic solver to the real and imaginary parts and combine; the resulting squared norm is the sum of the two real energy norms, with the stated sesquilinear pairing.

current_object.title: Spherical harmonics: orthogonal decomposition, complete basis and addition theorem
current_object.statement: Let $P_l$ denote the real vector space of homogeneous polynomials of degree $l$ on $\mathbb R^3$, $H_l=\ker(\Delta:P_l\to P_{l-2})$ with $P_k=\{0\}$ for $k<0$, and let spherical harmonics of degree $l$ be the restrictions of $H_l$ to $S^2$, with unnormalised surface measure $d\Omega$ of total mass $4\pi$. Then $P_l=H_l\oplus|x|^2P_{l-2}$, $\dim H_l=2l+1$, harmonics of distinct degree are orthogonal in $L^2(S^2,d\Omega)$, and the union over $l$ of the spaces of spherical harmonics admits a complete orthonormal basis of $L^2(S^2,d\Omega)$ ([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]). For any real orthonormal basis $Y_{lm}$, $m=1,\dots,2l+1$, of degree-$l$ harmonics the addition theorem holds: $$\sum_{m=1}^{2l+1}Y_{lm}(n)Y_{lm}(n')=\frac{2l+1}{4\pi}P_l(n\cdot n'),$$ where $P_l$ is the Legendre polynomial of the convergent zonal kernel lemma ([[lem-em-convergent-legendre-kernel]]). The Laplacian is the Euclidean one ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]). This supplies the harmonic decomposition, orthogonality, completeness and exact addition kernel; it does not assert higher boundary regularity.
current_object.strategy: For homogeneous $Q$ of degree $l-2j$, Euler's identity $x\cdot\nabla Q=(l-2j)Q$ gives $\Delta(r^{2j}Q)=2j(2l-2j+1)r^{2j-2}Q+r^{2j}\Delta Q$; the ansatz $H=\sum_ja_jr^{2j}\Delta^jP$ with $a_0=1$ and $a_j=-a_{j-1}/[2j(2l-2j+1)]$ cancels consecutive coefficients in $\Delta H$, and the final $\Delta^{\lfloor l/2\rfloor+1}P$ vanishes by degree, so $H$ is harmonic and $P-H$ is divisible by $r^2$; recursion gives the decomposition. For homogeneous harmonic $H_l,H_m$ the Green identity on the ball ([[cor-second-green-identity-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]]) gives $0=\int_{S^2}(H_l\partial_nH_m-H_m\partial_nH_l)=(m-l)\int_{S^2}H_lH_m$, whence orthogonality of distinct degrees; if a harmonic of degree $l$ equalled $r^2Q$, its orthogonality to all lower-degree harmonics would force $\int_{S^2}H_l^2=0$, so $H_l=0$; the monomial count $\dim P_l=(l+1)(l+2)/2$ gives $\dim H_l=2l+1$, and restriction is injective by the same homogeneity argument. For density, continuous functions are dense in $L^2(S^2)$ by a finite smooth graph atlas with subordinate smooth cutoffs, pulling each localised function back, mollifying and using the $L^2$ translation and approximate-identity interfaces ([[lem-complex-translation-and-approximate-identity-interfaces]]); the restricted real polynomial algebra is unital and separates points, so Stone-Weierstrass ([[thm-real-stone-weierstrass-general]]) makes it uniformly dense in $C(S^2)$, and the homogeneous-degree decomposition puts every restriction in the finite span of spherical harmonics, giving $L^2$ density. Finite Gram-Schmidt ([[thm-gram-schmidt-orthonormalisation]]) applied to a fixed ordered monomial elimination basis of each $H_l$ produces the orthonormal bases without an undefined basis selection. For the addition theorem, $K_l(n,n')=\sum_mY_{lm}(n)Y_{lm}(n')$ is independent of the orthonormal basis and rotation-invariant, and for fixed $n'$ it is the unique (up to scale) rotation-invariant homogeneous harmonic polynomial of degree $l$, which is the coefficient $|y|^lP_l(n'\cdot y/|y|)$ of the convergent kernel of the zonal lemma ([[lem-em-convergent-legendre-kernel]]); evaluating the diagonal by integrating $K_l(n,n)$ gives $(2l+1)/(4\pi)$, completing the addition theorem.

current_object.title: Three-dimensional radial Carleman inequality with integer weight
current_object.design_state: local-research-proof-written; exact-hypotheses-retained; not published and not engine-certified
current_object.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$). Let $s\ge1$ be an integer and put $\tau=s+1$. Write $r(x)=|x|$ for $x\in\mathbb R^3$ and let $\Delta$ be the Euclidean Laplacian ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]). Then for every $u\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\})$,
$$\|r^{-\tau}u\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^3)}\le\frac{2}{s}\,\|r^{-\tau+2}\Delta u\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^3)}.$$
Moreover, if $u\in H^2(\mathbb R^3)$ is compactly supported in an annulus $\{0<a\le|x|\le b\}$, then the weak second derivatives of $u$ exist as locally square integrable functions, $\Delta u$ denotes their sum in the weak sense ([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]), and the same inequality holds for $u$. The weight $r^{-\tau+2}$ is bounded on every fixed compact annulus but is not integrable at the origin, and this is exactly why the density extension is stated for functions whose support stays away from $r=0$. The constant $2/s$ is explicit and is not claimed to be sharp.
current_object.strategy:
Change of variables. Write $x=rn$ with $r=e^{-t}$, $t\in\mathbb R$, $n\in S^2$, and set $u(rn)=r^{-1/2}v(t,n)$, $w(t,n)=e^{st}v(t,n)$. The polar-coordinates formula ([[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]]) and the one-dimensional substitution ([[cor-one-dimensional-change-of-variables-with-absolute-derivative]]) give $dx=r^3\,dt\,d\sigma(n)$, and with $u^2=r^{-1}v^2$ and $\tau-1=s$,
$$\int_{\mathbb R^3}r^{-2\tau}u^2\,dx=\int_{\mathbb R}\int_{S^2}w^2\,d\sigma\,dt.$$
The radial computation ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]) $\Delta u=r^{-5/2}(\partial_t^2v+\Delta_{S^2}v-\tfrac14v)$ and the substitution $v=e^{-st}w$ give $\partial_t^2v=e^{-st}(\partial_t-s)^2w$; the same factor $e^{2st}$ occurs in $r^{-2\tau+4}(\Delta u)^2r^3\,dt\,d\sigma$, hence
$$\int_{\mathbb R^3}r^{-2\tau+4}(\Delta u)^2\,dx=\int_{\mathbb R}\int_{S^2}\bigl|\bigl((\partial_t-s)^2+\Delta_{S^2}-\tfrac14\bigr)w\bigr|^2\,d\sigma\,dt.$$
Modal decomposition. Expand $w(t,\cdot)$ for almost every $t$ in the complete orthonormal basis of spherical harmonics ([[lem-em-spherical-harmonic-basis-and-addition]]) and use the eigenvalue identity $\Delta_{S^2}Y_{lm}=-l(l+1)Y_{lm}$, a direct computation from the homogeneous extension: $H_l$ is a homogeneous harmonic polynomial and $\Delta=\partial_r^2+2r^{-1}\partial_r+r^{-2}\Delta_{S^2}$ gives $0=r^{-2}(l^2+l+\Delta_{S^2})H_l$. Parseval ([[thm-parseval-equivalences-for-a-complete-orthonormal-family]]) and monotone convergence identify the two displayed integrals with the sums of the modal norms $\sum_{l,m}\|w_{lm}\|^2$ and $\sum_{l,m}\|((\partial_t-s)^2-(l+\tfrac12)^2)w_{lm}\|^2$. Fourier multiplier. In the $2\pi$ convention of [[thm-fourier-differentiation-and-multiplication-identities-on-tempered-distributions]] and Plancherel ([[thm-plancherel]]) the mode operator has symbol $(2\pi i\xi-s)^2-(l+\tfrac12)^2$; with $x=4\pi^2\xi^2\ge0$, $A=s-l-\tfrac12$ and $B=s+l+\tfrac12$, its squared modulus is $(x+A^2)(x+B^2)$, which is increasing in $x\ge0$ and therefore at least $A^2B^2=(s^2-(l+\tfrac12)^2)^2$. For integers $l\ge0$ and $s\ge1$ the integer $l$ minimizing $|s^2-(l+\tfrac12)^2|$ is $l=s-1$ or $l=s$, with value $s-\tfrac14\ge\tfrac s2$, so the squared modulus is at least $s^2/4$. Hence $\|w_{lm}\|\le\tfrac2s\|((\partial_t-s)^2-(l+\tfrac12)^2)w_{lm}\|$ for every mode, and summing the nonnegative squared modal norms gives the inequality for smooth compactly supported $u$. Density extension. On a fixed annulus $a\le r\le b$ the weights $r^{\pm\tau}$, $r^{-\tau+2}$ are bounded. Approximate $u\in H^2(\mathbb R^3)$ with support in that annulus in the $H^2$ norm by $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ functions ([[cor-compactly-supported-smooth-functions-are-dense-in-wkp-of-rn]]), multiply each approximant by a smooth cutoff equal to one on a neighbourhood of the support of $u$ and vanishing near the origin ([[lem-smooth-bump-between-concentric-euclidean-balls]], [[lem-weak-leibniz-rule-with-a-smooth-factor]]); the products lie in $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\})$, still converge to $u$ in $H^2$, and because the weights are bounded on the fixed annulus both sides of the inequality pass to the limit. Countable Choice is declared because it is assumed by [[thm-plancherel]] and by the density corollary; no other choice principle is used.

current_object.strategy: First, for $|x|\ge2a$ and $\lambda_3$-a.e. $y$ one has $\rho(y)=0$ off $\overline B_a(0)$, while for $y\in\overline B_a(0)$ one has $|x-y|\ge r-a\ge r/2>0$ ([[lem-every-norm-on-rn-is-continuous-for-the-euclidean-metric]], [[def-metric-ball]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]); hence $|x-y|^{-1}\le2/r$ on the support and the integral against $\rho$ converges absolutely ([[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]], [[thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]], [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]], [[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]]). Since the kernel is bounded on the support and the support is $\lambda_3$-a.e. contained in $\overline B_a(0)$, the integral equals $N\rho(x)$ by the defining formula of [[def-newtonian-potential]] ([[thm-the-lebesgue-integral-respects-almost-everywhere-equality]]). Because $\Phi(z)=1/(4\pi|z|)$ for $n=3$ ([[pthm-em-coulomb-solution]] (c)), one has $N\rho(x)=(4\pi)^{-1}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\rho(y)|x-y|^{-1}\,d\lambda_3(y)$ and hence $\varphi(x)=(4\pi\varepsilon_0)^{-1}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\rho(y)|x-y|^{-1}\,d\lambda_3(y)$ for $r\ge2a$. current_object.title: External force and torque on a small neutral charge distribution in a slowly varying electrostatic field
current_object.strategy: Write $E_{\mathrm{ext}}(y)=E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)+\bigl(E_{\mathrm{ext}}(y)-E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)\bigr)$ $\lambda_3$-a.e. on the support and integrate term by term. For (a), the constant term of the force gives $\bigl(\int\rho\,d\lambda_3\bigr)E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)=QE_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)$, and the constant term of the torque gives $\bigl(\int\rho(y)\,y\,d\lambda_3(y)\bigr)\times E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)=p\times E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)$ by linearity of the integral on $L^1$ and the bilinearity of the cross product ([[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]], [[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]). For the force remainder, if $R_F\ne0$ test it against the unit vector $u:=R_F/|R_F|$: $|R_F|=u\cdot R_F=\int\rho(y)\,u\cdot\bigl(E_{\mathrm{ext}}(y)-E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)\bigr)d\lambda_3(y)\le\int|\rho(y)|\,|E_{\mathrm{ext}}(y)-E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)|\,d\lambda_3(y)\le L\int|y|\,|\rho(y)|\,d\lambda_3(y)\le La\|\rho\|_1$, using $u\cdot v\le|v|$ ([[thm-cauchy-schwarz-and-the-euclidean-norm]]), the triangle and monotonicity rules for the integral ([[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]], [[thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]) and $|y|\le a$ $\lambda_3$-a.e. on the support; the case $R_F=0$ is trivial. For the torque remainder, $\bigl|\int\rho(y)\,y\times\bigl(E_{\mathrm{ext}}(y)-E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)\bigr)d\lambda_3(y)\bigr|\le\int|\rho(y)|\,|y|\,|E_{\mathrm{ext}}(y)-E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)|\,d\lambda_3(y)\le L\int|y|^2|\rho|\,d\lambda_3\le La^2\|\rho\|_1$, using $|y\times v|\le|y|\,|v|$ ([[thm-cross-product-norm-is-the-two-vector-gram-determinant]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). Since the two integrals are absolutely convergent, all interchanges are finitely many applications of linearity and the triangle rule. For (b) insert $Q=0$. For (c), subtract and add $o$: $\int\rho(y)(y-o)\times E_{\mathrm{ext}}(y)d\lambda_3=\tau-o\times F$ by linearity and bilinearity of the cross product. For (d): at an instant of zero coordinate velocity the four-velocity has chart components $U=(c,0,0,0)$, hence $U_0=\eta_{0\mu}U^\mu=-c$ and $U_i=0$ ([[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]] (b),(c)); the adopted equation [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]] (i) then gives $m\,dU^i/d\tau=q'F^{i0}U_0=q'(-E_i/c)(-c)=q'E^i$ because $F^{i0}=-E_i/c$ ([[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] (a)). Summing the two instantaneous forces and computing the moments about the origin by finite sums gives the displayed force and torque, with $p=q(d/2)+(-q)(-d/2)=qd$ by [[def-em-electric-moments]] (c) and the bound $|R_\tau|\le|q|\,(a)\,(2La)=2|q|La^2$; the same expansion as (a) applies with the total variation $2|q|$ ([[def-finite-sum]], [[lem-finite-sum-laws]]). Clause (e) records the model assumptions. Countable Choice is used only through the Lebesgue integrals and their suppliers; the Lipschitz constant and the field values enter only through the displayed estimates, and the norm continuity of [[lem-every-norm-on-rn-is-continuous-for-the-euclidean-metric]] is used to read the pointwise bounds. Changing $\rho$ on a $\lambda_3$-null set changes no integral ([[thm-the-lebesgue-integral-respects-almost-everywhere-equality]]).

current_object.title: Convergent all-order spherical multipole expansion with monopole, dipole and quadrupole terms
current_object.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), inherited from the cited Lebesgue, spherical-harmonic and Newtonian interfaces ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $a>0$ and let $\rho\in L^1(\mathbb R^3)$ be real and vanish $\lambda_3$-a.e. outside $\overline B_a(0)$ ([[def-metric-ball]], [[def-measure-null-set-and-almost-everywhere]]); let $Q$, $p$ and $Q_{ij}$ be the total charge, dipole moment and traceless quadrupole of $\rho$ about the chart origin ([[def-em-electric-moments]] (a)); let $\varphi:=\varepsilon_0^{-1}N\rho$ be the potential of [[pthm-em-coulomb-solution]] (c) with the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]]; and let $\{Y_{lm}:l\ge0,\ m=1,\dots,2l+1\}$ be a real orthonormal basis of spherical harmonics of $L^2(S^2,d\sigma)$ of degree $l$, with $d\sigma$ the surface measure of total mass $4\pi$ and the addition theorem of [[lem-em-spherical-harmonic-basis-and-addition]] ([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). For every $l,m$ define the **spherical multipole moment of degree $l$**
$$q_{lm}:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}|y|^l\,Y_{lm}(y/|y|)\,\rho(y)\,d\lambda_3(y),$$
absolutely convergent because $|Y_{lm}|\le((2l+1)/(4\pi))^{1/2}$ on $S^2$ by the addition theorem and $|y|\le a$ $\lambda_3$-a.e. on the support, so the integrand is dominated by $a^l((2l+1)/(4\pi))^{1/2}|\rho|$ ([[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]], [[thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]). Write $x=rn$ with $r=|x|$ and $n\in S^2$. Then:
(a) [Exterior spherical multipole expansion] for every $x$ with $r>a$,
$$\varphi(x)=\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\sum_{l=0}^{\infty}\sum_{m=1}^{2l+1}\frac{4\pi}{2l+1}\,\frac{Y_{lm}(n)}{r^{l+1}}\,q_{lm},$$
the series converging absolutely and uniformly on $\{|x|\ge r_0\}$ for every $r_0>a$, with the tail after degree $N$ bounded by
$$\Bigl\|\,\varphi-\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\sum_{l=0}^{N}\sum_{m=1}^{2l+1}\frac{4\pi}{2l+1}\frac{Y_{lm}(n)}{r^{l+1}}q_{lm}\Bigr\|_{\infty,\{|x|\ge r_0\}}\le\frac{\|\rho\|_1\,a^{N+1}}{4\pi\varepsilon_0\,r_0^{N+2}\,(1-a/r_0)};$$
(b) [Monopole, dipole and quadrupole terms] the degree-$0$ and degree-$1$ terms of (a) are the monopole and dipole terms $Q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0r)$ and $p\cdot x/(4\pi\varepsilon_0r^3)$, and for $r\ge2a$ the difference between $\varphi$ and the truncation after degree $1$ obeys the remainder bound of [[pthm-em-electric-dipole-expansion]]; the degree-$2$ term equals the traceless-quadrupole term
$$\frac{1}{8\pi\varepsilon_0r^3}\,n_iQ_{ij}n_j;$$
(c) [Regularity and termwise differentiation] $\varphi$ is of class $C^\infty$ on $\{|x|>a\}$, the series in (a) may be differentiated termwise to every order, the differentiated series converging uniformly on every compact subset of $\{|x|>a\}$; in particular the field $E:=-\nabla\varphi$ of [[def-em-fields]] equals $-\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\sum_{l,m}\frac{4\pi}{2l+1}\nabla_x\bigl(Y_{lm}(n)r^{-l-1}\bigr)q_{lm}$ on $\{|x|>a\}$, with the same uniform convergence on compact subsets;
(d) [Scope] the hypotheses are a real compactly supported $L^1$ density and the exterior region $r>a$; no claim is made on or inside $\overline B_a(0)$, no convergence at $r=a$ is asserted, the theorem is not asserted for point or singular sources, and no empirical content is involved. The expansion is the exterior expansion of the potential of the static source $\rho$ read in the fixed-time dictionary of [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] (e).
current_object.strategy:
Scale the spherical multipole expansion of [[thm-em-spherical-multipole-basis]] (a)-(b) by the constant $(4\pi\varepsilon_0)^{-1}$, exactly as in [[pthm-em-electric-dipole-expansion]]: since $N\rho(x)=(4\pi)^{-1}\int\rho(y)|x-y|^{-1}d\lambda_3(y)$ for the observation points considered, $\varphi=(4\pi\varepsilon_0)^{-1}\int\rho(y)|x-y|^{-1}d\lambda_3(y)$, and part (a) of the supplier gives the displayed series, its absolute and uniform convergence on exterior regions, and the stated tail bound, all multiplied by the constant $(4\pi\varepsilon_0)^{-1}$ ([[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]] for scaling the integral, [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]], [[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]]). The coefficients $q_{lm}$ are absolutely convergent by the addition theorem's bound $\sum_{m=1}^{2l+1}Y_{lm}(n)^2=(2l+1)/(4\pi)$ of [[lem-em-spherical-harmonic-basis-and-addition]], which gives $|Y_{lm}|\le((2l+1)/(4\pi))^{1/2}$, and by $|y|\le a$ on the support ([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]). For (b): the degree-$0$ and degree-$1$ identifications and the remainder bound are parts of the supplier's clause (a) (with $Q=\int\rho$, $p=\int y\rho(y)d\lambda_3(y)$ and the bound $16a^2\|\rho\|_1/|x|^3$ for $|x|\ge2a$), scaled by $(4\pi\varepsilon_0)^{-1}$, and they reproduce [[pthm-em-electric-dipole-expansion]] (a). For the degree-$2$ term, use the addition theorem at $l=2$: $\sum_mY_{2m}(n)Y_{2m}(y/|y|)=\frac{5}{4\pi}P_2(n\cdot y/|y|)$, so that
$$\sum_{m=1}^{5}Y_{2m}(n)q_{2m}=\frac{5}{4\pi}\int_{\mathbb R^3}|y|^2P_2\Bigl(n\cdot\frac{y}{|y|}\Bigr)\rho(y)\,d\lambda_3(y),$$
and the second Legendre polynomial is fixed by the defining identity $(1-2qz+q^2)^{-1/2}=\sum_{l\ge0}q^lP_l(z)$ of [[lem-em-convergent-legendre-kernel]]: the coefficient of $q^2$ in the Taylor expansion of the left side at $q=0$ is $\frac12\frac{d^2}{dq^2}(1-2qz+q^2)^{-1/2}\big|_{q=0}=\frac{3z^2-1}{2}$ (the first and second derivatives computed by the chain rule, [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]]), while that coefficient on the right side is $P_2(z)$ (uniqueness of Taylor coefficients, [[def-taylor-polynomial-and-remainder]], [[lem-taylor-polynomial-derivatives]]); hence $P_2(z)=(3z^2-1)/2$. Therefore $|y|^2P_2(n\cdot y/|y|)=\bigl(3(n\cdot y)^2-|y|^2\bigr)/2$, and
$$\sum_{m=1}^{5}Y_{2m}(n)q_{2m}=\frac{5}{8\pi}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\bigl(3(n\cdot y)^2-|y|^2\bigr)\rho(y)\,d\lambda_3(y)=\frac{5}{8\pi}\,n_iQ_{ij}n_j$$
by the definition of $Q_{ij}$ in [[def-em-electric-moments]] (a) and linearity of the integral; the degree-$2$ term of (a) is then $\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\cdot\frac{4\pi}{5}\cdot\frac{1}{r^3}\cdot\frac{5}{8\pi}n_iQ_{ij}n_j=\frac{n_iQ_{ij}n_j}{8\pi\varepsilon_0r^3}$. For (c): part (b) of [[thm-em-spherical-multipole-basis]] gives that $\varphi$ is $C^\infty$ on $\{|x|>a\}$ and that the series may be differentiated termwise to every order with uniform convergence of each differentiated series on compact subsets; the displayed field series is the termwise gradient, with [[def-em-fields]] for the field object. The fixed-time dictionary is [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] (e). All estimates use the triangle and monotonicity rules for the Lebesgue integral ([[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]], [[thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]), the $\lambda_3$-a.e. support convention ([[def-measure-null-set-and-almost-everywhere]], [[thm-the-lebesgue-integral-respects-almost-everywhere-equality]]) and the declared Countable Choice of the measure, harmonic and Newtonian interfaces; no convergence at $r=a$ and no point-source assertion is made.

current_object.title: Far-field dipole expansion of a compact conserved current with a uniform explicit remainder
current_object.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), with the exact meaning of [[def-countable-choice]]. Let $J\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ with $\operatorname{div}J=0$ and $\operatorname{supp}J\subset B_a(0)$ for some $a>0$, let $A$ be the vector potential of [[pthm-em-magnetostatic-vector-potential]] and $B=\operatorname{curl}A$ its magnetostatic field, and let $m=\frac12\int_{\mathbb R^3}y\times J(y)\,dy$ be the magnetic moment of [[def-em-magnetic-moment]](a). Then for $r=|x|\ge2a$, uniformly in the unit vector $n=x/r$,

$$A(x)=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\frac{m\times x}{r^3}+O\!\left(\frac{\mu_0a^2\|J\|_1}{r^3}\right),\qquad B(x)=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\frac{3n(m\cdot n)-m}{r^3}+O\!\left(\frac{\mu_0a^2\|J\|_1}{r^4}\right),$$

where $\|J\|_1=\int_{\mathbb R^3}|J|\,d\lambda_3$ and the constants implicit in the $O$ terms are absolute: one constant works for all $r\ge2a$ and all unit $n$. This is a controlled two-term far-field estimate: nothing is asserted for $r<2a$ or at the support, no higher multipole is defined here, and the leading dipole term is not claimed to be exact.
current_object.strategy: **Proof technique:** transport of the explicit uniform-remainder lemma to the framework's objects. 1.1 The hypotheses of [[lem-em-magnetic-dipole-remainder]] are exactly those stated here for $J$ (smooth, compactly supported, divergence-free, contained in $B_a(0)$), and the objects of that lemma, $A=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\int J(y)|x-y|^{-1}dy$ and $B=\operatorname{curl}A$, are verbatim the $A$ and $B$ of [[pthm-em-magnetostatic-vector-potential]]; the moment $m=\frac12\int y\times J(y)\,dy$ of the lemma is the moment of [[def-em-magnetic-moment]](a) ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]]). 2.1 Substituting these identifications into the lemma's conclusion gives the displayed estimates for the framework's $A$ and $B$, with the lemma's uniformity in $n$ and its absolute constants; no additional analysis is required. 2.2 Scope: the estimate is a remainder-controlled far-field expansion; nothing is asserted at smaller radii or at the source, and no empirical content is added. The far-field identification of $m$ as the source moment is exactly the content of this theorem under its hypotheses. Countable Choice is inherited through the cited measure, surface, regular-distribution and/or Newtonian supplier interfaces; no stronger choice axiom is used in this argument. The magnetic-moment definition uses a finite Riemann integral on a closed bounding rectangle, whereas the remainder supplier writes the Lebesgue integral. Each smooth compact component of $y\times J(y)$ is bounded Borel and continuous on that rectangle, so [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]], under the stated Countable Choice, equates them; zero extension gives the same all-space Lebesgue moment.

current_object.title: Origin shift of the source moments: $Q$, the dipole $p-Qb$, the Cartesian expansion and the traceless quadrupole
current_object.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), inherited from the Lebesgue interface ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $a>0$ and let $\rho\in L^1(\mathbb R^3)$ be real and vanish $\lambda_3$-a.e. outside $\overline B_a(0)$, or let $(x_k,q_k)_{k=1}^N$ be a finite system of stationary point charges, with the source moments of [[def-em-electric-moments]] branches (a) and (c) respectively. For $b\in\mathbb R^3$ define the moments **about the reference point $b$** by replacing, in each integrand of [[def-em-electric-moments]] (a) and in each summand of (c), the vector $y$ by $y-b$ (respectively $x_k$ by $x_k-b$):
$$Q^{(b)}:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\rho\,d\lambda_3,\quad p^{(b)}:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}(y-b)\,\rho(y)\,d\lambda_3(y),\quad M^{(b)}_{i_1\dots i_l}:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\prod_{r=1}^l(y-b)_{i_r}\,\rho(y)\,d\lambda_3(y),$$
$$Q^{(b)}_{ij}:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\bigl(3(y-b)_i(y-b)_j-|y-b|^2\delta_{ij}\bigr)\rho(y)\,d\lambda_3(y),$$
and analogously with finite sums $M^{(b)}_{i_1\dots i_l}=\sum_{k=1}^N q_k\prod_{r=1}^l(x_k-b)_{i_r}$ in the point-charge branch. Every displayed integral is absolutely convergent: $\lambda_3$-a.e. on the support the monomials obey $|y_{i_1}\cdots y_{i_l}|\le a^l$ and, for $y-b$, $|y-b|^l\le(|y|+|b|)^l$ and $|3(y-b)_i(y-b)_j-|y-b|^2\delta_{ij}|\le4(|y|+|b|)^2$, so the integrands are dominated by constants times $|\rho|\in L^1$ ([[def-em-electric-moments]] (a), [[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]], [[thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]). Then:
(a) $Q^{(b)}=Q$ for every $b$;
(b) $p^{(b)}=p-Qb$, so the dipole moment is independent of the reference point exactly when $Q=0$;
(c) for every $l\ge0$,
$$M^{(b)}_{i_1\dots i_l}=\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\dots,l\}}(-1)^{|S|}\Bigl(\prod_{r\in S}b_{i_r}\Bigr)M_{(i_r:\,r\notin S)},$$
where $M_{(i_r:\,r\notin S)}$ is the Cartesian moment whose index list is the complement of $S$ and the empty index list is read as $Q$; in particular
$$M^{(b)}_{ij}=M_{ij}-b_ip_j-b_jp_i+b_ib_jQ;$$
(d) $Q^{(b)}_{ij}=Q_{ij}-3\bigl(b_ip_j+b_jp_i\bigr)+2(b\cdot p)\delta_{ij}+\bigl(3b_ib_j-|b|^2\delta_{ij}\bigr)Q$; consequently, if $Q=0$ and $p=0$, then $Q^{(b)}_{ij}=Q_{ij}$ for every $b$ (the traceless quadrupole of a neutral, non-dipolar distribution is independent of the reference point);
(e) [Scope] this is an exact identity between the declared source moments of [[def-em-electric-moments]]; it asserts nothing about fields, forces, dynamics or nature, and the reference point is a choice of coordinate origin, not an operation performed on the source.
current_object.strategy:
The theorem is the expansion of the polynomial $\prod_{r=1}^l(y_{i_r}-b_{i_r})$ followed by termwise integration (or summation). For (a) and (b) the degrees $0$ and $1$ are immediate; constant multiples of $\rho$ and of $y_i\rho$ pass through the integral by linearity of the Lebesgue integral on $L^1$ ([[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]]), and the finite-sum branch by linearity of finite sums ([[def-finite-sum]], [[lem-finite-sum-laws]]). For (c), expand by finite distributivity,
$$\prod_{r=1}^l(y_{i_r}-b_{i_r})=\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\dots,l\}}(-1)^{|S|}\Bigl(\prod_{r\in S}b_{i_r}\Bigr)\Bigl(\prod_{r\notin S}y_{i_r}\Bigr),$$
an identity of real polynomials proved by induction on $l$ (finitely many distribution steps, [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]] for the polynomial calculus), and integrate term by term: each monomial is dominated $\lambda_3$-a.e. by $a^l|\rho|$ on the support, hence absolutely integrable by [[def-em-electric-moments]] (a), so the finitely many applications of linearity are legitimate and the constants $\prod_{r\in S}b_{i_r}$ factor out ([[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]], [[thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]). For (d), multiply the case $l=2$ by $3$ and subtract $\delta_{ij}\sum_kM^{(b)}_{kk}$, using $Q^{(b)}_{ij}=3M^{(b)}_{ij}-\delta_{ij}\sum_kM^{(b)}_{kk}$, $Q_{ij}=3M_{ij}-\delta_{ij}\sum_kM_{kk}$ and $\sum_kM^{(b)}_{kk}=\sum_kM_{kk}-2b\cdot p+|b|^2Q$; this gives the displayed identity, and its four $b$-dependent terms vanish identically when $Q=0$ and $p=0$. Replacing $\rho$ by an equal $\lambda_3$-a.e. density changes no integral ([[thm-the-lebesgue-integral-respects-almost-everywhere-equality]]). The finite-sum branch repeats the same algebra with sums. No Choice beyond the declared $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is used; (e) records the scope.

current_object.title: Weak unique continuation for bounded potentials in three dimensions
current_object.design_state: local-research-proof-written; exact-hypotheses-retained; not published and not engine-certified
current_object.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$). Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be nonempty, open and connected, let $V\in L^\infty_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$, and let $\psi\in H^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ satisfy $\Delta\psi=V\psi$ in the distributional sense: $\int_\Omega\psi\,\Delta\varphi\,dx=\int_\Omega V\psi\,\varphi\,dx$ for every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$, with $\Delta\varphi$ the classical Laplacian. Here $H^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ denotes the locally integrable classes on $\Omega$ whose weak derivatives of every order at most two exist and are locally square integrable ([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]); $V\in L^\infty_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ means $V$ is measurable and $\|V\|_\infty<\infty$ on every compact subset ([[def-essential-supremum-with-respect-to-a-measure]], [[def-l-infinity-on-a-measure-space]]). If $\psi=0$ on a nonempty open subset of $\Omega$, then $\psi=0$ on $\Omega$. No smoothness, sign, symmetry or decay hypothesis on $V$ beyond local essential boundedness is used, and no analyticity is assumed.
current_object.strategy:
Local propagation step. Let $z\in\Omega$ be a point on a neighbourhood of which $\psi=0$, and let $R>0$ with $\overline B_R(z)\subseteq\Omega$; translate the origin to $z$ so that the weight of the Carleman lemma is measured from $z$. Choose $\chi\in C_c^\infty(B_R(0);[0,1])$ with $\chi=1$ on $B_{R/2}(0)$ ([[lem-smooth-bump-between-concentric-euclidean-balls]]) and put $u=\chi\psi$. By the smooth-factor Leibniz rule with $|\alpha|\le2$ ([[lem-weak-leibniz-rule-with-a-smooth-factor]]) $u$ has weak derivatives up to order two in $L^2(\mathbb R^3)$, is compactly supported in $B_R(0)$ and vanishes near $0$; since $\Delta\psi=V\psi$ distributionally, $\Delta u=Vu+e$ with $e=2\nabla\chi\cdot\nabla\psi+(\Delta\chi)\psi$, supported in the annulus $\{R/2\le|x|\le R\}$. Apply the radial Carleman lemma with parameter $s\ge4MR^2$, where $M=\|V\|_\infty$ on $B_R$ ([[def-essential-supremum-with-respect-to-a-measure]]): using $r\le R$ on the ball and $|V|\le M$, $\|r^{-\tau}Vu\|\le MR^2\|r^{-\tau}u\|$, and the lemma plus absorption of the term $\tfrac12\|r^{-\tau}u\|$ gives
$$\|r^{-\tau}u\|_2\le\frac4s\|r^{-\tau+2}e\|_2.$$
For $0<\rho<R/2$ one has $u=\psi$ on $B_\rho(0)$ and $r^{-\tau}\ge\rho^{-\tau}$ there, while $e$ is supported where $r\le R$, so
$$\|\psi\|_{L^2(B_\rho(0))}\le\rho^{\tau}\|r^{-\tau}u\|_2\le\frac{4R^2}{s}\Bigl(\frac{2\rho}{R}\Bigr)^{\tau}\|e\|_2\longrightarrow0\qquad(s\to\infty),$$
as $e$ is fixed. Hence $\psi=0$ on $B_{R/2}(z)$: vanishing near a point propagates to the ball of half the radius of any ball around that point that is relatively compact in $\Omega$. Global propagation. Let $Z$ be the union of the open sets on which $\psi$ vanishes; $Z$ is open and nonempty by hypothesis. Fix $x\in\Omega$ and a polygonal path $\gamma:[0,1]\to\Omega$ from a point of $Z$ to $x$, which exists because $\Omega$ is a connected open subset of $\mathbb R^3$ ([[def-connected-space]], [[cor-components-of-open-subsets-of-rn-are-polygonally-connected]], [[def-polygonal-path-and-polygonal-connectedness]]). The image $\gamma([0,1])$ is compact and disjoint from the closed set $\mathbb R^3\setminus\Omega$, so it has distance $\delta>0$ from it ([[lem-relative-compact-closed-sets-have-a-positive-distance-gap]]). By uniform continuity of $\gamma$ on $[0,1]$ choose $0=t_0<\dots<t_N=1$ with $|\gamma(t_{j+1})-\gamma(t_j)|<\delta/4$. Inductively, if $\psi=0$ near $\gamma(t_j)$, then $B_{\delta/2}(\gamma(t_j))$ has closure in $\Omega$, so the propagation step with $R=\delta/2$ gives $\psi=0$ on $B_{\delta/4}(\gamma(t_j))$, a neighbourhood of $\gamma(t_{j+1})$; hence $\psi=0$ near $x=\gamma(t_N)$. As $x\in\Omega$ was arbitrary, $Z=\Omega$. Consequently $\Omega\setminus Z$, which is open in $\Omega$, is empty: otherwise $Z,\Omega\setminus Z$ would be a separation of $\Omega$ ([[def-connected-space]]). This proves $\psi=0$ on $\Omega$. Countable Choice is inherited through the Carleman lemma; no further choice principle is used.

current_object.title: Exterior spherical multipole expansion and the ball boundary series
current_object.statement:
Let $a>0$ and let $\rho\in L^1(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R)$ vanish outside $\overline B_a(0)$. Use the complete orthonormal basis $\{Y_{lm}\}$ of real spherical harmonics on $S^2$ with unnormalised surface measure $d\sigma$ of total mass $4\pi$ and the addition theorem of [[lem-em-spherical-harmonic-basis-and-addition]], and the Legendre generating kernel and its compact remainder bound from [[lem-em-convergent-legendre-kernel]]. Write $x=rn$, $r=|x|$, $n\in S^2$. Then:
(a) **Exterior multipole expansion.** For every $x$ with $|x|>a$,
$$\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{\rho(y)}{|x-y|}\,dy=\sum_{l=0}^\infty\sum_{m=1}^{2l+1}\frac{4\pi}{2l+1}\frac{Y_{lm}(n)}{r^{l+1}}\int_{\mathbb R^3}|y|^lY_{lm}(y/|y|)\rho(y)\,dy,$$
the series converging absolutely and uniformly on $\{|x|\ge r_0\}$ for every $r_0>a$, with tail after degree $N$ bounded by $\|\rho\|_1\,a^{N+1}/(r_0^{N+2}(1-a/r_0))$; the degree-$l$ term is the $L^2(S^2)$ projection of $y\mapsto|x-y|^{-1}\rho(y)$ onto the degree-$l$ harmonics. The degree-zero and degree-one terms are the Coulomb and dipole terms with the explicit remainder bound of [[lem-em-coulomb-dipole-remainder]] ($Q=\int\rho$, $p=\int y\rho(y)\,dy$, $|R(x)|\le16a^2\|\rho\|_1/|x|^3$ for $|x|\ge2a$).
(b) **Termwise differentiation.** On every compact $K$ with $\inf_K|x|>a$ the series may be differentiated termwise to every order, the differentiated series converging uniformly on $K$; in particular the potential is $C^\infty$ on $\{|x|>a\}$.
(c) **Ball boundary branch.** For $f\in L^2(S^2)$ with coefficients $f_{lm}$ the series $u(rn)=\sum_{l,m}r^lf_{lm}Y_{lm}(n)$ converges in $L^2(S^2)$ as $r\uparrow1$ and, with all derivatives, uniformly on each closed ball of radius $<1$, is harmonic on the open unit ball, and is the unique harmonic function there with a finite $\sup_{r<1}\|u(r\cdot)\|_2$ and $L^2$ boundary limit $f$; for continuous $f$ it equals the Poisson integral $(1-r^2)/(4\pi|rn-n'|^3)$ of $f$ and extends continuously to the closed ball with boundary values $f$. This is a statement about the Newtonian integral of a compactly supported $L^1$ density and about harmonic functions; no physical charge distribution or electrostatic interpretation is asserted.
current_object.strategy: Assembly of the recorded branches. Write $q=|y|/r$ and $z=n\cdot y/|y|$ for $y\ne0$; the convergent Legendre kernel [[lem-em-convergent-legendre-kernel]] gives $|x-y|^{-1}=\sum_l(|y|^l/r^{l+1})P_l(z)$ for $|y|\le a<r$, with the stated geometric tail, and integration against the finite measure $\rho\,dy$ yields the zonal multipole series with the displayed error times $\|\rho\|_1$. Substituting the addition theorem $P_l(z)=\frac{4\pi}{2l+1}\sum_mY_{lm}(n)Y_{lm}(y/|y|)$ from [[lem-em-spherical-harmonic-basis-and-addition]] into the $l$-th term and separating variables gives the displayed spherical-harmonic coefficients, the finite sums agreeing with the zonal series for every degree, hence in the uniform limit. The degree-zero and degree-one coefficients are $Q$ and the components of $p$, and comparison with the explicit Coulomb-dipole splitting of [[lem-em-coulomb-dipole-remainder]] (twice the fundamental theorem applied to $h(s)=|x-sy|^{-1}$) identifies the remainder and its bound. For (b), differentiate the zonal kernel with respect to the observation variable on a compact set disjoint from $\overline B_a$: the analytic integrand admits a complex parameter disk bounded away from its zeros, so Cauchy estimates bound each fixed spatial derivative of the $l$-th term by a polynomial in $l$ times $(a/r_0)^l$ ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]); the ratio test gives uniform convergence of the differentiated series, and the harmonic/integral representations identify the limit with the corresponding derivative, using the inner product conventions of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]] and the differentiability framework of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]. For (c), the addition theorem gives $\sum_m|Y_{lm}(n)|^2=(2l+1)/4\pi$, so Cauchy-Schwarz bounds the absolute tail at fixed $r<1$ by $\|f\|_2(\sum_{l>N}r^{2l}(2l+1)/4\pi)^{1/2}\to0$; the derivative estimates and the interior harmonic estimates of [[lem-em-ball-poisson-series-boundary-convergence]] give uniform convergence of all derivatives on smaller balls, orthogonality gives $\|u(r\cdot)-f\|_2\to0$, and the radial ODE argument quoted there (two solutions $r^l$, $r^{-l-1}$, smoothness at the centre excluding the second) gives uniqueness in the stated class; the Poisson kernel identity and uniform boundary convergence for continuous $f$ are the last part of that lemma. Completeness and orthonormality of the basis are those of [[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]].
